arxiv-2107-10199.title: Distribution of Classification Margins: Are All Data Equal?
arxiv-2107-10199.creator: Andrzej Banburski, Fernanda De La Torre, Nishka Pant, Ishana Shastri, Tomaso Poggio
arxiv-2107-10199.description: Abstract Recent theoretical results show that gradient descent on deep neural networks under exponential loss functions locally maximizes classification margin, which is equivalent to minimizing the norm of the weight matrices under margin constraints. This property of the solution however does not fully characterize the generalization performance.

arxiv-2312-13886.title: The Cosmological Constant Potential: a resolution to the Hubble tension via the cosmological sound horizon
arxiv-2312-13886.creator: Nima Khosravi
arxiv-2312-13886.description: Abstract The cosmological constant term can be seen as a constant potential for a (scalar) field. In this viewpoint, at late times, the field is stopped rolling and behaves as a cosmological constant ( w = − 1 w=-1 ).

arxiv-2312-14960.title: Numerical results on Quantum Energy Inequalities in Integrable Models at the Two-Particle level
arxiv-2312-14960.creator: Jan Mandrysch
arxiv-2312-14960.description: Abstract In this article, we study the impact of self-interaction and multi-particle states on sustaining negative energies in relativistic quantum systems. For physically reasonable models, one usually requires bounds on both magnitude and duration of the accumulation of negative energy, typically given in form of a Quantum Energy Inequality (QEI).

arxiv-2403-17960.title: On generalizations of Iwasawa’s theorem Thanks: This research was supported in part by Shandong Provincial Natural Science Foundation, China (ZR2017MA022) and NSFC (11761079). ∗∗ Corresponding author. E-mail addresses: shijt2005@pku.org.cn (J. Shi), xufj2023@s.ytu.edu.cn (F. Xu), shanmj2023@s.ytu.ed
arxiv-2403-17960.creator: Jiangtao Shi, Fanjie Xu, Mengjiao Shan School of Mathematics and Information Sciences, Yantai University, Yantai 264005, China
arxiv-2403-17960.description: Abstract Iwasawa’s theorem indicates that a finite group G G is supersolvable if and only if all maximal chains of the identity in G G have the same length. As generalizations of Iwasawa’s theorem, we provide some characterizations of the structure of a finite group G G in which all maximal chains of every minimal subgroup have the same length.

arxiv-2405-08324.title: Sufficient conditions, lower bounds and trade-off relations for quantumness in Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability
arxiv-2405-08324.creator: Agung Budiyono
arxiv-2405-08324.description: Abstract Kirkwood-Dirac (KD) quasiprobability is a quantum analog of classical phase space probability. It offers an informationally complete representation of quantum state wherein the quantumness associated with quantum noncommutativity manifests in its nonclassical values, i.e., the nonreal and/or negative values of the real part.

arxiv-2406-05540.title: A Fine-tuning Dataset and Benchmark for Large Language Models for Protein Understanding
arxiv-2406-05540.creator: Yiqing Shen, Zan Chen, Michail Mamalakis, Luhan He, Haiyang Xia, Tianbin Li, Yanzhou Su, Junjun He, Yu Guang Wang
arxiv-2406-05540.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yiqing Shen, Zan Chen, Michail Mamalakis, Luhan He, Haiyang Xia, Tianbin Li, Yanzhou Su, Junjun He, Yu Guang Wang. The high similarities between protein sequences and natural language, particularly in their sequential data structures, have driven parallel advancements in deep learning models for both domains.

arxiv-2409-12969.title: Seeing Through Their Eyes: Evaluating Visual Perspective Taking in Vision Language Models
arxiv-2409-12969.creator: Gracjan Góral, Alicja Ziarko, Michał Nauman, Maciej Wołczyk
arxiv-2409-12969.description: Abstract Visual perspective-taking (VPT), the ability to understand the viewpoint of another person, enables individuals to anticipate the actions of other people. For instance, a driver can avoid accidents by assessing what pedestrians see. Humans typically develop this skill in early childhood, but it remains unclear whether the recently emerging Vision Language Models (VLMs) possess such capability.

arxiv-2507-05139.title: CHIME/FRB Discovery of an Unusual Circularly Polarized Long-Period Radio Transient with an Accelerating Spin Period Facilities: CHIME, GBT, VLA, Swift(XRT and UVOT), HSC Numpy, Astropy, sigpyproc3, Presto
arxiv-2507-05139.creator: Fengqiu Adam Dong, Kaitlyn Shin, Casey Law, Mason Ng, Ingrid Stairs, Geoffrey Bower, Alyssa Cassity, Emmanuel Fonseca, B. M. Gaensler, Jason W. T. Hessels, Victoria M. Kaspi, Bikash Kharel, Calvin Leung, Robert A. Main, Kiyoshi W. Masui, James W. McKee, Bradley W. Meyers, Obinna Modilim, Ayush Pandh
arxiv-2507-05139.description: Abstract We report the discovery of CHIME J1634+44, a Long Period Radio Transient (LPT) unique for two aspects: it is the first known LPT to emit fully circularly polarized radio bursts, and it is the first LPT with a significant spin-up.

arxiv-2512-03070.title: Mixed Data Clustering Survey and Challenges
arxiv-2512-03070.creator: Guillaume Guerard, Sonia Djebali
arxiv-2512-03070.description: Abstract The advent of the big data paradigm has revolutionized the way industries handle and analyze information, ushering in an era characterized by unprecedented volumes, velocities, and varieties of data. In this context, mixed data clustering emerges as a critical challenge, necessitating innovative approaches to effectively harness the wealth of heterogeneous data types, including numerical and categorical variables.

pmc-10655062.title: Effects of cohort, genotype, variant, and maternal β-blocker treatment on foetal heart rate predictors of inherited long QT syndrome
pmc-10655062.creator: Alexander M Kaizer, Annika Winbo, Sally-Ann B Clur, Susan P Etheridge, Michael J Ackerman, Hitoshi Horigome, Ulrike Herberg, Federica Dagradi, Carla Spazzolini, Stacy A S Killen, Annette Wacker-Gussmann, Arthur A M Wilde, Elena Sinkovskaya, Alfred Abuhamad, Margherita Torchio, Chai-Ann Ng, Annika Ry
pmc-10655062.description: AimsIn long QT syndrome (LQTS), primary prevention improves outcome; thus, early identification is key. The most common LQTS phenotype is a foetal heart rate (FHR) < 3rd percentile for gestational age (GA) but the effects of cohort, genotype, variant, and maternal β-blocker therapy on FHR are unknown.

pmc-10733591.title: Prevalence of Iron Deficiency, Anemia, and Associated Factors in a Blood Donor Population in Brazzaville, Congo
pmc-10733591.creator: Firmine Olivia Galiba Atipo-Tsiba, Earl Quincy Gayaba Mouyabi, Brunel Monic Angounda, Serge Oscar Mokono, Lethso Thibaut Ocko Gokaba, Alexis Elira Dokekias
pmc-10733591.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Introduction Blood donation is not without risk to the donor. It results in a substantial loss of iron and decreased hemoglobin. In our country, no predonation assessment is carried out and the selection of blood donors is only clinical. Objectives To determine the prevalence of iron deficiency, anemia, and iron deficiency anemia and to identify the factors associated with anemia and iron status in a blood donor population at the National Center for Blood Transfusion (NCBT).

pmc-11448221.title: Improving role allocation for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in the emergency department: a quality improvement project
pmc-11448221.creator: Sweta Giri, Dawa Gyeltshen, Neten Wangchuk, Kinley Dorji, Loday Drakpa, Sonam Wangdi, Kiran Biswa Diyali
pmc-11448221.description: IntroductionIn any healthcare setting, cardiopulmonary resuscitations (CPRs) stand out as demanding and chaotic resuscitation endeavours. Emergency departments (EDs) witness a significant volume of CPRs. Given the critical nature of CPR, content knowledge and procedural skills alone fall short in delivering optimal care. Effective teamwork, complemented by a well-coordinated response, is imperative for achieving favourable patient outcomes.

pmc-11468403.title: A deep learning model to enhance the classification of primary bone tumors based on incomplete multimodal images in X-ray, CT, and MRI
pmc-11468403.creator: Liwen Song, Chuanpu Li, Lilian Tan, Menghong Wang, Xiaqing Chen, Qiang Ye, Shisi Li, Rui Zhang, Qinghai Zeng, Zhuoyao Xie, Wei Yang, Yinghua Zhao
pmc-11468403.description: BackgroundAccurately classifying primary bone tumors is crucial for guiding therapeutic decisions. The National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines recommend multimodal images to provide different perspectives for the comprehensive evaluation of primary bone tumors. However, in clinical practice, most patients’ medical multimodal images are often incomplete.

pmc-11471232.title: Chemical profiling, bioactive compounds, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory activities of Indonesian propolis extract produced by Tetragonulalaeviceps
pmc-11471232.creator: Muhammad Yusuf Abduh, Tri Ramadianti Shafitri, Elfahmi Elfahmi
pmc-11471232.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Propolis produced by stingless bees contains various chemical compounds that contribute to its bioactivity. The availability of certain plants at the growth site and the propolis's geographic origin have a significant impact on its chemical composition. The objective of this study was to examine the chemical profile, yield, total flavonoid and phenolic content, and in vitro antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of propolis extract from 10 distinct locations in Indonesia.

pmc-12775146.title: Human monoclonal antibodies that target clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 hemagglutinin
pmc-12775146.creator: Garazi Peña Alzua, André Nicolás León, Temima Yellin, Disha Bhavsar, Madhumathi Loganathan, Kaitlyn Bushfield, Philip J. M. Brouwer, Alesandra J. Rodriguez, Trushar Jeevan, Richard Webby, Christine Marizzi, Julianna Han, Andrew B. Ward, J. Andrew Duty, Florian Krammer
pmc-12775146.description: The highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus clade 2.3.4.4b has been spreading globally since 2022, causing mortality and morbidity in domestic and wild birds, as well as in mammals, which underscores its potential to cause a pandemic. Here, we generate a panel of anti-hemagglutinin (HA) human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against the H5 protein of clade 2.3.4.4b.

pmc-13651362.title: Quantitative CMR-derived pulmonary circulation imaging biomarkers in recent-onset dilated cardiomyopathy associated with pulmonary hemodynamics and clinical improvement
pmc-13651362.creator: Lukáš Opatřil, Mary Luz Mojica-Pisciotti, Roman Panovský, Jan Máchal, Tomáš Holeček, Věra Feitová, Július Godava, Hana Poloczková, Vladimír Kincl, Jan Krejčí
pmc-13651362.description: BackgroundRecent-onset dilated cardiomyopathy (RODCM), defined as new DCM with heart failure (HF) symptoms appearing within six months, is a less documented form of HF. This study aims to evaluate pulmonary circulation imaging biomarkers (PCIB) obtained by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with RODCM to assess their association with pulmonary hypertension, systolic and diastolic function, and clinical improvement.
